questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.8

Circle problem 1 compares a circle of radius 6 to a circle of radius 6. Which transformation proves similarity?

feedback.text: A translation changes location but not radius.

answer.text: A dilation with scale factor 2, possibly after a rigid motion

feedback.text: A dilation maps one radius length to the other, and a rigid motion can align centers.
A reflection preserves size and cannot change radius.
A dilation gives a valid similarity transformation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.5

Circle problem 2 has an inscribed angle intercepting a 92° arc. What is the angle measure?

feedback.text: That is the central angle relationship, not the inscribed angle relationship.
This doubles instead of halves the arc.
The intercepted arc measure is enough information.
An inscribed angle measures half its intercepted arc.

questiontext.text:

feedback.text: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
Opposite angles are not necessarily congruent.
This does not use the 180° sum.
A right angle is not guaranteed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.4

Circle problem 4 has a tangent length t and a secant with external segment 7 and whole length 28. What is t?

feedback.text: Adding lengths does not use the tangent-secant theorem.
This is t?, not t.
Use t? = external times whole, so t = 14.
The tangent-secant relationship gives enough information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.1

Construction problem 5 asks for a circumscribed circle of a triangle. Which construction locates its center?

feedback.text: Angle bisectors locate the incenter.

answer.text: Perpendicular bisectors of the triangle sides

feedback.text: The circumcenter is the intersection of perpendicular bisectors.
One median does not locate the circumcenter.
A tangent construction does not locate the circumscribed-circle center.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.2

Construction problem 6 asks for a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle. What supports the equal side construction?

answer.text: Stepping the radius around the circle creates six equal chords.

feedback.text: A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle has side length equal to the radius.

answer.text: Using the diameter as each side

feedback.text: The diameter is too long to be each side.
The vertices must be equally spaced.
Tangents are outside contact lines, not inscribed sides.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.3

Construction problem 7 draws a tangent from an external point. What must be true at the point of tangency?

answer.text: The tangent passes through the center.

feedback.text: A line through the center is not tangent at the circle.

answer.text: The tangent intersects the circle twice.

feedback.text: That describes a secant.
Tangent length is not defined by matching the diameter.

answer.text: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.

feedback.text: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U05_L07_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CIR.7

Measurement problem 8 has radius 8 and central angle 80°. Which expression gives sector area?

feedback.text: This is arc length, not sector area.
This is full circumference.
Sector area is the central-angle fraction of circle area.
This is full circle area, not the sector area unless the angle is 360°.
